problem_statement:
Admin doesn't display properly unicode chars in JSONFields.
Description
	 
		(last modified by ZhaoQi99)
	 
>>> import json
>>> print json.dumps('中国')
"\u4e2d\u56fd"
json.dumps use ASCII encoding by default when serializing Chinese.
So when we edit a JsonField which contains Chinese character in Django admin,it will appear in ASCII characters.
I have try to fix this this problem in ​https://github.com/adamchainz/django-mysql/pull/714.And it works prefectly.
evidence_shown:
FAIL: test_json_display_for_field (admin_utils.tests.UtilsTests) (value={'a': '你好 世界'})
AssertionError: '{"a": "\u4f60\u597d \u4e16\u754c"}' != '{"a": "你好 世界"}'
- {"a": "\u4f60\u597d \u4e16\u754c"}
+ {"a": "你好 世界"}

FAIL: test_prepare_value (forms_tests.field_tests.test_jsonfield.JSONFieldTest)
AssertionError: '"\\u4f60\\u597d\\uff0c\\u4e16\\u754c"' != '"你好，世界"'
- "\u4f60\u597d\uff0c\u4e16\u754c"
+ "你好，世界"

Ran 35 tests in 0.114s
FAILED (failures=2)
reviewer_reasoning: The issue is that JSONField values are dumped with ASCII escapes, causing Chinese characters to display as \u sequences in the admin. Changing JSONField.prepare_value to use json.dumps(..., ensure_ascii=False) outputs real Unicode characters. This is the correct place in the forms pipeline used by the admin. The failing tests shown expect the non-escaped output and will pass with this change. No other regressions are implied since encoding remains handled by the existing encoder. Thus the patch fully resolves the ticket.
